arxiv-1810-07398.title: A Study of Curvature Theory for Different Symmetry Classes of Hamiltonian
arxiv-1810-07398.creator: Y R Kartik, Ranjith R Kumar, S Rahul, Sujit Sarkar
arxiv-1810-07398.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Y R Kartik, Ranjith R Kumar, S Rahul, Sujit Sarkar. We study and present the results of curvature for different symmetry classes (BDI, AIII and A) model Hamiltonians and also present the transformation of model Hamiltonian from one distinct symmetry class to other based on the curvature property. We observe the mirror symmetric curvature for the Hamiltonian with BDI symmetry class but there is no evidence of such behavior for Hamiltonians of AIII symmetry class.

arxiv-2105-05707.title: The ionization of carbon at 10-100 times the diamond density and in the 10 6 K temperature range.
arxiv-2105-05707.creator: M. W. C. Dharma-wardana
arxiv-2105-05707.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. W. C. Dharma-wardana. The behaviour of partially ionized hot compressed matter is critical to the study of planetary interiors as well as for nuclear fusion studies. A recent quantum study of carbon in the 10-70 Gbar range and at a temperature of 100 eV used N N -atom density functional theory (DFT) with N ∼ 32 N\sim 32 -64 and molecular dynamics (MD). This involves band-structure type electronic calculations and averaging over many MD generated ion configurations.

arxiv-2203-13046.title: Facial Action Unit Recognition With Multi-models Ensembling
arxiv-2203-13046.creator: Wenqiang Jiang, Yannan Wu, Fengsheng Qiao, Liyu Meng, Yuanyuan Deng, Chuanhe Liu
arxiv-2203-13046.description: Abstract 1 Abstract The Affective Behavior Analysis in-the-wild (ABAW) 2022 Competition gives Affective Computing a large promotion. In this paper, we present our method of AU challenge in this Competition. We use improved IResnet100 as backbone. Then we train AU dataset in Aff-Wild2 on three pertained models pretrained by our private au and expression dataset, and Glint360K respectively.

arxiv-2304-10566.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hannah Klion, Revathi Jambunathan, Michael E. Rowan, Eloise Yang, Donald Willcox, Jean-Luc Vay, Remi Lehe, Andrew Myers, Axel Huebl, Weiqun Zhang. Relativistic magnetic reconnection is a non-ideal plasma process that is a source of non-thermal particle acceleration in many high-energy astrophysical systems. Particle-in-cell (PIC) methods are commonly used for simulating reconnection from first principles.

arxiv-2409-07865.title: Transit Timing Variation of K2-237b: Hints Toward Planet Disk Migration
arxiv-2409-07865.creator: Fan Yang, Richard J. Long, Eamonn Kerins, Supachai Awiphan, Su-Su Shan, Bo Zhang, Yogesh C. Joshi, Napaporn A-thano, Ing-Guey Jiang, Akshay Priyadarshi, Ji-Feng Liu
arxiv-2409-07865.description: Abstract Hot Jupiters should initially form at considerable distances from host stars and subsequently migrate towards inner regions, supported directly by transit timing variation (TTV). We report the TTV of K2-237b, using reproduced timings fitted from Kepler K2 and TESS data. The timings span from 2016 to 2021, leading to an observational baseline of 5 years.

arxiv-2504-13855.title: Bio-crafting Architecture: Experiences of growing mycelium in minimal surface molds
arxiv-2504-13855.creator: Anca-Simona Horvath, Alina Elena Voinea, Radu Arie s , an
arxiv-2504-13855.description: Abstract This study documents a three-week workshop with architecture students, where we designed and 3D printed various minimal surfaces using wood-based filaments, and used them as molds in which to grow mycelium. We detail the design process and the growth of the mycelium in different shapes, together with participants’ experiences of working with a living material.

arxiv-2507-14655.description: Abstract In this article we propose an extension to the typed natural deduction calculus TNDPQ to model verification of counterfactual fairness in probabilistic classifiers. pmc-10518001.creator: Meriem Merah, Chahra Boudoukha, Antonio Avalos Ramirez, Mohamed Fahim Haroun, Samira Maane
pmc-10518001.description: The valorization of paper mill sludge (PMS) is the main goal of this study. The emissions of PMS continue to increase at global scale, especially from packaging paper and board sectors. The raw sludge was used to prepare an adsorbent to remove toxic pollutants from wastewater, the methylene blue (MB), an organic dye.

pmc-10667756.title: Isolated synovial chondromatosis of the ankle: A case report
pmc-10667756.creator: Rafik Elafram, Majdi Sghaier, Majdi Ben Romdhane, Ahmed Hamdi
pmc-10667756.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Introduction and importanceAt the age of 20, young adults are most susceptible to synovial chondromatosis, a rare condition characterized by the metaplasia of the synovial membrane into cartilaginous or osteocartilaginous tissue. Synovial chondromatosis is exceptionally uncommon in the ankle.Case presentationAn orthopedist evaluated a 26-year-old man with a history of recurring ankle trauma over a period of 6 months, swelling and pain. An ankle radiograph revealed calcified foreign bodies, while arthrography displayed enlarged oval bodies with contrasting features and intra-articular effusion encapsulated heterogeneously.

pmc-11355009.title: A Simple Expression for the Screening of Excitonic Couplings between Chlorophylls as Inferred for Photosystem I Trimers
pmc-11355009.creator: Matthias Eder, Thomas Renger
pmc-11355009.description: The Coulomb coupling between transition densities of the pigments in photosynthetic pigment-protein complexes, termed excitonic coupling, is a key factor for the description of optical spectra and energy transfer. A challenging question is the quantification of the screening of the excitonic coupling by the optical polarizability of the environment.

pmc-11430096.title: Utility of Quantitative EEG in Neurological Emergencies and ICU Clinical Practice
pmc-11430096.creator: Misericordia Veciana de las Heras, Jacint Sala-Padro, Jordi Pedro-Perez, Beliu García-Parra, Guillermo Hernández-Pérez, Merce Falip
pmc-11430096.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The electroencephalogram (EEG) is a cornerstone tool for the diagnosis, management, and prognosis of selected patient populations. EEGs offer significant advantages such as high temporal resolution, real-time cortical function assessment, and bedside usability. The quantitative EEG (qEEG) added the possibility of long recordings being processed in a compressive manner, making EEG revision more efficient for experienced users, and more friendly for new ones.

pmc-12504114.title: EEG-based brain connectivity and sentiment analysis from smartphone social communication: insights into remitted major depressive disorder among adolescents
pmc-12504114.creator: Nayoung Kim, Lilian Y Li, Carter J Funkhouser, Allison M Letkiewicz, Esha Trivedi, Aishwarya Sritharan, Sarah Elizabeth Sarkas, Madeline Marie McGregor, Katherine Durham, David Pagliaccio, Alva Tang, Nicholas B Allen, Stewart A Shankman, Randy P Auerbach
pmc-12504114.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Although prior research has identified abnormal brain connectivity in remitted depressed adolescents, there is limited work associating these alterations with real-time affective dynamics, which may shed insight about specific biological markers that contribute to depression recurrence. Effective brain connectivity was estimated using renormalized partial directed coherence (rPDC) from resting-state EEG data collected in adolescents (N = 144; ages 13–18), including youth with remitted depression (n = 85) and healthy controls (n = 59).

pmc-12524466.title: The Etiological Role of Impaired Neurogenesis in Schizophrenia: Interactions with Inflammatory, Microbiome and Hormonal Signaling
pmc-12524466.creator: Miu Tsz-Wai So, Ata Ullah, Abdul Waris, Fahad A. Alhumaydhi
pmc-12524466.description: Schizophrenia is a prevailing yet severely debilitating psychiatric disorder characterized by a convoluted etiology. Although antipsychotics have been available for over half a century, they primarily mitigate symptoms rather than providing definitive care. This limitation suggests that the neurotransmitter systems targeted by these medications are not the root cause of the disorder.

pmc-12589597.title: Reduced aerosol pollution diminished cloud reflectivity over the North Atlantic and Northeast Pacific
pmc-12589597.creator: Knut von Salzen, Ayodeji Akingunola, Jason N S Cole, Ruth A R Digby, Sarah J Doherty, Luke Fraser-Leach, Edward Gryspeerdt, Michael Sigmond, Robert Wood
pmc-12589597.description: Over the past several decades, the proportion of solar radiation reflected back into space has declined, accelerating the accumulation of heat within the Earth system. Here we show that the marine cloud reflectivity decreased on average by 2.8 ± 1.2% per decade in the combined North Atlantic and Northeast Pacific regions between 2003 and 2022.

pmc-13043405.title: Hidden diagnoses among patients with double seronegative myasthenia gravis
pmc-13043405.creator: Vukan Ivanovic, Stojan Peric, Caitlin Briggs, Ana Marjanovic, Jovan Pesovic, Ivana Basta, Johan Jansson, Simrat Randhawa, Sonja Rajic, Sankalp Gokhale
pmc-13043405.description: IntroductionDouble seronegative myasthenia gravis (dSnMG) is defined as myasthenia gravis (MG) without detectable antibodies to acetylcholine receptor (AChR) and muscle-specific kinase (MuSK). Absence of a disease-specific biomarker and clinical heterogeneity can significantly complicate diagnostic pathway. This study aimed to identify cases misdiagnosed as dSnMG.MethodologyThe study included 33 patients [64% females, median age at onset 30 (22.

pmc-13048093.title: Nanohydrogels for Diabetic Wound Healing: Mechanisms, Applications, and Future Perspectives
pmc-13048093.creator: Jinyuan Wu, Jiaqi Gu, Xueping Wu
pmc-13048093.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Diabetic wound healing remains a significant clinical challenge, characterized by persistent hyperglycemia, chronic inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and recurrent infections. Traditional wound dressings often fail to address the complex pathological microenvironment of diabetic wounds. Nanohydrogels, particularly nanohybrid systems such as polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS)-based hydrogels, metal-organic framework (MOF) nanozyme hydrogels, and zinc-based polyoxometalate (Zn-POM) hydrogels, have emerged as advanced multifunctional platforms for diabetic wound repair.

pmc-13431615.title: Effects of Dietary Pomegranate Syrup Supplementation on Growth Performance, Carcass Traits, Meat Quality, Oxidative Stress, and GPx7 Gene Expression in Japanese Quail (Coturnix coturnix japonica)
pmc-13431615.creator: Aydin Daş, Besime Doğan Daş, Mücahit Kahraman, Mehmet Avci, Akın Yiğin, Sadik Serkan Aydin, Gülüzar Şengül, Oğuz Ağyar, Ahmet Yusuf Şengül
pmc-13431615.description: Simple SummaryThis study examined the effects of adding pomegranate syrup (0.0%, 0.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3%) to the diets of Japanese quail on growth performance, meat quality, and antioxidant status. A total of 120 quails were used and divided into four groups. The results showed that feed intake and meat quality traits were not affected by supplementation.

pmc-13660985.title: KSHV K15 genetic heterogeneity is associated with Kaposi sarcoma aggressiveness through modulation of the host inflammatory microenvironment
pmc-13660985.creator: Yu Zhang, Peng Wang, Jingzhan Zhang, Yunying Wang, Tingting Li, Yuan Ding, Xiaojing Kang
pmc-13660985.description: Kaposi sarcoma (KS) exhibits profound clinical heterogeneity, yet current risk assessment remains constrained by anatomical staging systems that lack universality across diverse KS variants. This study characterized the functional impact of Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) K15 genotypes (M or P) on clinical aggressiveness in a retrospective cohort of 156 patients from Xinjiang, China.

pmc-13677732.title: Oncogenic mutations in non-small cell lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to clinical practice
pmc-13677732.creator: Chaozhuo Li, Xiaoyan Yin, Shujie Zhou, Junxu Wen, Jinming Yu, Xiangjiao Meng
pmc-13677732.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Targeted therapy has revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients harboring oncogenic alterations, and next-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) significantly increase blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, leading to improved disease control and survival benefits. However, several issues remain to be addressed, including the selection of more appropriate and individualized agents, the emergence of TKI resistance, and the challenging management of central nervous system (CNS) progression.
